title: A stack class in two files
description:
Build a small class across a header and a source file, the way real projects are laid out. `IntStack.h` is finished; write the member functions in `IntStack.cpp`.

| Member | Does |
|---|---|
| `void push(int value)` | puts a value on top |
| `bool pop()` | removes the top value; returns `false` (and does nothing) if the stack is empty |
| `int top() const` | the top value; if the stack is empty, returns 0 |
| `bool empty() const`, `std::size_t size() const` | |

starter.IntStack.cpp:
#include "IntStack.h"

// Define the five member functions here.

hints: In `IntStack.cpp`, include the header first and write each member with the class name in front: `void IntStack::push(int value) { ... }`.
Check for an empty stack in `pop` and `top` before touching the vector inside.
lessonTitle: Classes in Header Files and Nested Types
